about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one.
title: Nation States game design review

messages.text:
Read through the entire prompt before starting.

You are a professor with a PhD in Game Design and teach masters level classes of game design that focuses on turn based computer games. As per your contract with the university you work at, you are allowed and encourage to take on freelance work as a game design  consultant.

I am hiring you as a consultant on my game idea that I am developing.

The way that you do your consulting is that you first analyze my brief located at "C:\Users\aaron\Nation States\DESIGN.md" and then go through the rest of the code in the folder and then give it a grade if it was a project that I was submitting as my final project in your masters level class on video games. You give it two grades out of 100 based on the rubric you created for this.

There are going to be two different grades that you will give. The first grade will be on the technical side of things - how well is it coded/organized/balanced/etc. The second grade will be on the story/game play mechanics (note - if the gameplay mechanics in idea are great but poorly executed they will get a good grade here but less grade in the technical side of things.)

Then after giving it a grade you put together a brief explaining what works that I've already pointed out, what is working that I probably don't realize is working, what isn't working that I pointed out, what isn't working that I haven't noticed yet, overall feasibility of my short term goals (create a map based game that on its own is a full game) and long term goals (sell the game via kickstarter/steam/other markets), what changes you would make to the game and why, and then finally a market feasiabilty study that includes estimated cost to produce vs how much I would be able to sell it for, what the interest in this kind of game would be, similiar/comprable games in both the mainstread and indie game world, what changes I could make to make it more viable in the market, and then finally a final grade on the game as a whole that determines where the game ranks:

s - this game will be a popular indie game that breaks out of the indie game market and become a mainstream hit
a - this is a game that will be a hit in the gaming world and the kind of game that will develop a following (e.g. subreddit where people talk about strategy etc) and when a DLC is released the DLC will sell well
b - this is a game that could do a successful kickstarter or steam launch and find some success after it. It won't be a huge hit but it will be something that will do alright and if I were to make another game people would say, "the guy who made Nation States made this new game - I'll give it a try".
c - this is a game that will have a successful kickstarter and those people will enjoy it but it won't go that far after that.
d - if this gets a successful kickstarter/steam launch it will be more to due with my abilities in marketing than the quality of the game. Most people who get it will play it once or twice but then forget about it. 
e - this is a game that is great for me to learn about game design but it won't go past that and won't reach a market outside of people I know
f - the inherint premise of the game is broken and to fix it would change the game so much that it would be unrecognizable from what it is now and it is best to start over.

Remember in this scenario I am paying you for your knowledge in the game world and you do not know me as a friend so you will be honest with me.

Your findings should also give a general summary of the game, your favorite part of it, and any additional information or thoughts that you have about the idea.

After those findings you will then propose the future road map for the game and how to improve it. That roadmap should include steps/prompts for my programmer to take and then know what they need to create/code to implement it.

This is all great but I think there are some updates that we need to make before we get there. Because this story is built around this idea of individual nations we need to incorporate that idea. 

The idea is that the game will start out with texas falling apart as five nations:

* Dallas (which is the subregion dallas)
* Houston (subregion houston)
* El Paso (subregion El Paso)
* Austin (subregion Austin)
* San Antonio (subregion san antonio and hidalgo)


California also needs to break up into the following states with smaller "city states":

* Los Angeles as it's own
* Bay Area (marin county, sonoma county, napa county, solano county, contra costa county, alameda county, santa clara county, san mateo county, san francisco county)
* Riverside (riverside county, imperial county, san bernadino)
* SoCal (culture sub region minus the what has laready seperated)
* Northern California (minus everything already seperated)


The part of california that is in the sub-region Cascadia will become cascadia and the cascadian and state of jefferson movements need to become larger in areas.

Parts of the Mormon Corridor will cede as Deseret that will be based on RNG but the areas of the Mormon Corridor that didn't cede should have increased sepratist sentiment and it should grow faster than others.

Can you put together a plan to implement all of these things first before we move onto the union audit?
